LESSON: WRITING 9.4.1 PUNCTUATION (THE COMMA)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma), part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Which five wild animals are found in Kenya? 2. How do we decide where to pause when reading a text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  Recognise commas from a text on wall charts/chalk board/ digital and print resources. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light.  Use comma correctly in writing exercises, with peers.  Use commas to write lists of items/ names, with peers. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Collaboration: Teamwork is enhanced as the learner actively participates in role play conversations with peers observing the rules

of engagement.

Values:
Love is enhanced as the learner portrays a caring attitude towards the peers as they work together.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is nurtured as they use of the commas in writing.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner is able to comma correctly in writing lists of items in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.
